correctness.rationale: Positive-weight phase alignment reduces spatial numerical radius over real or complex ell_p to an exact simplex maximum. Weighted AM-GM makes the uniform point the unique unperturbed global maximizer. The simplex-tangent Hessian is -n(p-1)/p^2 times the cycle Laplacian, strictly negative on zero-mean variations; compactness and analytic implicit-function theory ensure the global maximum has a unique analytic mass profile. Taylor expansion gives b=alpha*h+beta*backshift(h), and commuting circulant identities reduce b^T L^+ b to h^T L^+ h-alpha*beta||h||^2. The mode eigenvalues of L are 4sin^2(pi*k/n), proving every nonnegative curvature coefficient and the stated equality cases. The four-cycle difference follows from exactly 1/2 and 1/4 Green energies. The packaged verifier is a finite numerical check, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This determines the full positive-semidefinite Hessian of a natural operator invariant on the complete finite-cycle weight space, for every finite dimension and real Banach exponent 1<p<infinity. The inverse-Laplacian kernel yields structurally informative mode sensitivity and identifies the unique Hilbert/alternating flat regime, rather than an arbitrary numerical constant. It gives a universal p-independent relative local ordering for matched-mean, matched-variance weight placements, with an explicit four-cycle strict rearrangement effect. Such local sensitivity is motivated by the published cyclic weight-permutation optimization problem.
